card.title: The Cleanup Person
card.instruction: Return to the familiar role of containing damage, correcting stories, and protecting everyone from the consequences of disclosure.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you explain the broken window to Mum, give me your versions. Like last time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said football. Jamie said the wind.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we start with the broken window and our offer to pay. Leave weather out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Jamie already texted her about a storm.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll text her our offer to pay before she asks which storm plays football.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 resumes the familiar story-containment role, A3 focuses the account on damage and payment, and A5 sends that offer before the conflicting storm claim attracts questions.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's competing versions inform A3's common-ground message; B4's already-sent storm text causes A5 to send the payment offer immediately.

relationship.evidence: B2 gives the actual accounts and B4 supplies a relevant disclosure already made by Jamie.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's timing to enact the previously proposed damage-control message without a new prop.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes the broken window and intended explanation to Mum; B2-B4 make the story conflict clear.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's storm-playing-football question is earned by B2's two versions and B4's escalation to a storm.
